judge_verdict.summary: The agent shipped correct Python-level enum and kwarg fast-path optimizations (~1.7x on the primary benchmark) but fell well short of the reference Rust enum commit and the 1.1 speedup threshold.

verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a fair agent-fault failure: the verifier correctly rejected the rollout because the continuous reward 0.763 fell below the 1.1 pass threshold and opt_commit was false [1][2][3]. The task asked for maximum enum-benchmark speedup while preserving identical validation outputs [4], and the hidden harness grades patch speed against reference commit ac9e6ee (Move enum validation and serialization to Rust) using the gm_speedup_patch_commit metric [5][6]. The agent made a substantive attempt—fast-pathing to_enum via _value2member_map_ in _std_types_schema.py and skipping default-kwarg forwarding in TypeAdapter/BaseModel validators [7]—and every post-patch gso_test run passed functional equivalence checks [8], but on the primary enum workload (Test 0) mean time dropped only from ~0.100s to ~0.058s (~1.73x) versus ~0.039s (~2.55x) for the reference commit, leaving the patch ~32% slower than the target solution [9]. The agent's own bench.py self-check (~0.058s) confirmed a real but incomplete gain and did not establish parity with the Rust commit bar it could not see [10], so the task was not genuinely accomplished under GSO's performance gate even though correctness was preserved.
